title: Population change since 1970 by bird group (percent)

source.name: Decline of the North American avifauna
source.publisher: Rosenberg et al., Science (Cornell Lab of Ornithology / American Bird Conservancy)

notes: Grassland birds lost 53% of their population (largest proportional loss of any biome); shorebirds lost roughly 37%. Wetland birds were the only biome to gain overall, led by a 56% increase in waterfowl -- credited to decades of wetland restoration funded by hunting license and duck stamp fees plus the 1972 DDT ban.
